ev: The no-zombie half of this fact is now TEST-ASSERTED, which is precisely what every one of these five drift verdicts was falsifying. Built 2026-08-05, one probe per stack, each in the stack's own existing live test so it inherits that test's capability gate: the child PID is read through a named observability seam on the transport, the process is PROVED alive first (else the probe would be checking emptiness), the wrapper is DROPPED rather than shut down gracefully — so the kill-on-drop backstop is what gets exercised, against a live and uncooperative child — and the OS process table is polled to a deadline until the PID is gone, with a recycled PID read as dead by comparing `start_time`.

Go: `dropping_the_oracle_kills_the_gopls_child_no_zombie` in `go-ai-native-tcg-bridge/tests/live_oracle.rs`. It COMPILES here and is not claimed to have run — the Go oracle needs gopls, and this stack's posture is to fail with a recipe on a box that lacks it rather than skip. The assertion exists; running it is the toolchain's business, which is what «test-asserted» means for a capability-gated live test.
Measured before building, and it held: no such assertion existed in any of the three stacks — the tree's only process-table probe belonged to fractality and was about a different child.
